title: Push a wafer boat into an oxidation furnace with the push rod at 1 ft/min until the rod's white band meets the door
instruction: Push the boat to the middle of the furnace tube with the push rod, at about 1 ft per minute (1 inch every 5 seconds), holding the rod only on the cold side of its white band (the side toward its blunt back end), until the white band is flush with the furnace door plate. The stroke is longer than one arm's reach, so you may pass the rod from one hand to the other, but never stop the push for long. Do not touch the boat or the wafers. Then draw the rod straight back out without moving the boat, lay it on both rests of the holder with its hook facing up, and move both hands clear.
context: Thermal oxidation grows the gate and field oxide on silicon wafers, so furnace loading is chip lab work. Unlike TK-2CQX43 (sample boats in a materials-research furnace), this is silicon wafer oxidation in a horizontal tube furnace, loaded by hand on a long quartz push rod, as university and industry R&D cleanrooms still do (Georgia Tech IEN, Texas A&M AggieFab and Boise State SOPs, in the README). The boat goes in slowly, about 1 ft per minute, so the wafers do not crack from thermal shock: the rod's white band stops flush with the furnace door, hands stay on the cold side of the band, and the rod goes back in its holder hook up. The push is a steady 5 mm/s held for two minutes against the boat's sliding friction. The 61 cm stroke is longer than one arm's travel, so the push may be passed from one hand to the other (the way the demo does it; not scored). The hard part is that slow, steady, long push with a 1 m rod, not a choice or a reading.
setup: Station: two YAM arms, bases 61 cm apart. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Furnace tube: a clear acrylic tube, 150 mm bore and 1.2 m long, along y with its axis at x 40, 15 cm above the table, from y +50 to +170, on two stands; a flat floor inside it, with a side rail 60 mm either side of the axis. A plywood door plate (12 mm thick, 60 x 45 cm, a 150 mm hole on the tube's axis) stands across the mouth, its face at y +50. A red ring on the tube marks the hot zone where the boat's middle ends (y +120.5). Boat: quartz-style, 150 mm long (along y) and 110 mm wide, 25 slots at 4.76 mm holding 25 wafers 100 mm across and 525 um thick (9.6 g each), 0.39 kg loaded; a lug across its near end carries a pushing cup (two cheeks 12 mm apart) for the rod's tip. It sits on the tube floor just inside the mouth, its lug at y +52. Boat on the tube floor: friction 0.3, about 1.2 N to slide. Push rod: quartz, 10 mm across, 1,000 mm long, 0.17 kg, a white band 630 mm from its furnace end and a small hook on top 25 mm from that end. It lies on its holder, two V-rests (45 degree faces, a 35 mm mouth) on the tube's axis line at x 40, one at y -42 under its back part and one at y +46 just before the door; its axis is then 8.3 cm above the table, its tip in the boat's cup at y +52, hook up, and the white band at y -11, 61 cm from the door plane. Pushed until the band is flush with the door, the boat's lug is at y +113 and its middle at the hot-zone ring. Drawn back out and laid in the holder, the rod's tip rests on the front V-rest between y +46.5 and +49. Real trial, cold: a clear 1.2 m acrylic tube of 150 mm bore on two stands with a plywood door plate; a 10 mm fused-quartz rod 1 m long (0.17 kg; CVD Equipment makes push/pull rods) with a painted band and a fused hook; two V-blocks; a 25-slot quartz boat (Thasar EQ-QB series) with 25 reclaim wafers. Parts about USD 120.
scoring: Measured from the video against a tape along the rod's path and at the door. Score 0 if a hand ever holds the rod on the furnace side of the white band, a hand touches the boat, the boat tips, or any 2 s of the push moves the boat faster than 12 mm/s. 0.25: the boat pushed 10 cm into the tube. 0.5: the white band within 6 mm of the door plane. 0.75: and the push's mean speed (distance over time, from the boat's first motion to the band reaching the door; a hand-change pause under 10 s is allowed) from 3.8 to 6.4 mm/s (0.75 to 1.25 ft/min) with no stop longer than 10 s. 1.0: and the rod drawn out (its tip at least 1 cm outside the door plane) with the boat moved under 5 mm by it, lying in both holder V-rests with the hook up (within 45 degrees of vertical), hands 8 cm clear, everything still for 1 s.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. Sizes, masses and the band's place are SOP and SEMI M1 values; the rod is solid quartz, 0.17 kg. The tube is a flat floor and two side rails (box colliders) under a clear cylinder; boat friction 0.3 static, 0.25 sliding; rails 0.05, for the smooth wall. The 25 wafers are fixed in the boat. No heat: thermal shock is scored by push speed. The cameras cannot see the boat inside the tube, as in a real furnace; the scorer reads its final position from the simulator.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 on GPU physics, filmed. Dream-1: 0.0 (one valid run, 4,800 steps).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials pull the boat back to the mouth and lay the rod on its start rest with its end against the lug.
